question: A 27-year-old man with seizure disorder is brought to the emergency department by his girlfriend after falling while climbing a building. The girlfriend reports that he was started on a new medication for treatment of depressed mood, low energy, and difficulty sleeping 2 weeks ago by his physician. She says that he has had unstable emotions for several months. Over the past 3 days, he has not slept and has spent all his time “training to climb Everest.” He has never climbed before this period. He also spent all of his savings buying mountain climbing gear. Physical examination shows ecchymoses over his right upper extremity, pressured speech, and easy distractibility. He is alert but not oriented to place. Which of the following drugs is the most likely cause of this patient's current behavior?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "27-year-old man with seizure disorder" -> "started on new medication for depression" -> "symptoms of mania observed" -> "unstable emotions, lack of sleep, pressured speech" -> "possible side effect of bupropion" -> "bupropion can induce manic episodes in predisposed individuals" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient exhibits manic symptoms" -> "ecchymoses and risky behavior noted" -> "spending all savings on climbing gear" -> "bupropion associated with increased energy and impulsivity" -> "bupropion is a stimulant-type antidepressant" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Girlfriend reports new medication started 2 weeks ago" -> "patient has not slept for 3 days" -> "engaging in excessive goal-directed activity" -> "bupropion can lead to manic episodes" -> "most likely cause of current behavior" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient's behavior includes pressured speech and distractibility" -> "these are symptoms of mania" -> "new antidepressant could trigger mania" -> "bupropion is known to cause such effects" -> "most likely drug causing current behavior" -> 88%
analysis: The patient's symptoms suggest a manic episode, characterized by elevated mood, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, and impulsive behavior (spending all savings on climbing gear). Bupropion is known to potentially induce mania in susceptible individuals, especially those with a history of bipolar disorder or mood instability. Given that he was started on a new medication for depression and has shown signs of mania, bupropion is the most likely cause of his current behavior.
